How to Learn

Seekhne ka tareeqa

Learn in the right order. Do not skip steps. Free learning comes first, then the course, then mentorship.

1

Learn free from YouTube

Watch the full free playlist on YouTube. It teaches the full process from zero. Start here before you spend money on any course.

2

Take the course

Follow the modules on this site. Each module has short lessons in simple English and Urdu. Learn one module, then move to the next one.

3

Take mentorship

After the course, learn from a mentor. Mentorship saves time and corrects mistakes early. You can also buy a paid course after you learn the basics from YouTube. Do not buy a course first.

Module 1: Introduction to Etsy

Etsy kya hai

What Etsy is. How it started. What sells on Etsy. Why digital products are a good start.

  • What is Etsy?
  • The history of Etsy: it started in June 2005, in a Brooklyn apartment, built by Rob Kalin, Chris Maguire and Haim Schoppik. Jared Tarbell joined them later.
  • What sells on Etsy: handmade items, vintage items, craft supplies and digital products.
  • Why our focus is digital products.
  • How Etsy earns money: listing and selling fees (exact fees to be checked on Etsy).

Lesson 1.1: What is Etsy?

Etsy is an online marketplace. It works like Daraz, Amazon and eBay. Buyers search for products and buy them. Sellers list products and send the orders to buyers. You can sell from Pakistan. You need an account, a product and a way to receive payments.

Etsy ek online marketplace hai. Buyer search kar ke khareedta hai, seller list kar ke bechta hai.

Lesson 1.2: Four things you can sell

There are four ways to sell on Etsy.

  • Physical products: real items like furniture. Shipping from Pakistan is hard and costly. This is a separate topic.
  • Print on demand: you design, and a company like Printify or Printful prints and ships it. You do not keep stock. A shirt can sell for about $15.
  • Dropshipping: the buyer orders from you, and the supplier ships the item. You keep the margin. Note: Etsy does not allow dropshipping. This needs a separate lesson.
  • Digital products: you make a file once and sell it again and again. Planners, templates and Excel sheets are examples. There is no shipping, no stock and no return to handle.

Etsy par chaar cheezein bech sakte hain: physical, print on demand, dropshipping aur digital products.

Lesson 1.3: Why digital products first

Digital products are the best start. You make the file once and sell it for life. There is no shipping and no return problem. Even $2 or $3 per sale is good, because there is no work after the sale. Print on demand is second. Physical products are hard because of shipping and returns. A simple example: a $5 product that sells 7 times a day earns about $35 a day. That is an example, not a promise.

Digital product ek dafa banao aur baar baar becho. Is mein shipping aur return ka masla nahi hota.

Lesson 1.4: Evergreen and seasonal products

Some products sell all year. These are evergreen products. Some products sell only in a season. Q4 means October, November and December. It is the best season for sales. Halloween, Christmas and Ramadan shopping come in this time. Learn both types before you choose a product.

Evergreen product saal bhar bikta hai. Seasonal product sirf season mein bikta hai. Q4 sab se achha season hai.

Lesson 1.5: White hat, grey hat and black hat

White hat means clean work. Sell your own real products. Follow the steps one by one. Give one hour a day. Build slowly toward $500 a month. Black hat means fast money with wrong products, like copied brands. Sales come fast, but Etsy removes the account. Grey hat means replica products. If Etsy catches you, the account is gone. Start with white hat only.

White hat ka matlab hai saaf tareeqe se kaam karna. Black hat aur grey hat se account band ho sakta hai.

Lesson 1.6: Mindset

Learn slowly and apply slowly. Do not try to do everything at once. Follow one mentor and one track. Do not keep changing direction. Do not tell people you are learning Etsy before you have sales. People will ask questions and you will have no answers. Orders can take days or months. Do not panic. Keep working. Build a good circle of people who help you grow.

Aahista seekho aur aahista apply karo. Ek mentor aur ek track par chalo.

Lesson 1.7: Protect your account

Five basics protect your account. One: one IP, one account. If two accounts run on the same Wi-Fi, Etsy can disable both. Two: if you ever make a second account, keep everything separate. Three: your withdrawal details must match your CNIC and your Etsy account name. In Pakistan, payment comes through Payoneer. Create and verify Payoneer well before you link it. Four: never upload copied designs or images. Five: know the fees before you start. These are the basics taught in the lesson. Check the official Etsy rules too.

Account bachane ke liye paanch basics yaad rakho: ek IP par ek account, details CNIC se match karein, Payoneer pehle se verify karein, aur copied design kabhi upload na karein.

Lesson 1.8: Fees

The lesson states these fees. Account setup fee in Pakistan is $19, one time. Listing fee is $0.20 per listing. There is also an optional subscription of $10 per month, which gives free listings. Sale fees are separate and come in a later lesson. Pay the $19 fee with a card in the same name as the account. Do not pay from someone else's account. Fees can change, so check the current fees on Etsy before you publish.

Fees badal sakti hain. Publish karne se pehle Etsy par current fees check karein.

Source: Free YouTube playlist (Class 1), Etsy Seller Handbook.

Module 1 lesson added

Module 2: Account Setup

Account setup

Who can sell on Etsy. How to open a shop. How sellers in Pakistan receive payments.

  • Which countries can open an Etsy shop.
  • How to open a shop, step by step.
  • Pakistan: Payoneer and payout options.
  • Other banks and payout methods.
  • Shop settings: language, country and currency.
  • Common mistakes in account setup.

Lesson 2.1: Prepare before you start

Prepare before you start. Do not create two Etsy accounts on the same IP address. Use the same name on everything: account, documents, bank and Payoneer. Use a separate internet connection. Reset the modem. If you use a mobile hotspot, reset the mobile too. Use a fresh Chrome profile for this account, separate from any profile used before. Use a separate laptop if you can.

Shuru karne se pehle tayyari karein. Ek IP par ek account, har jagah ek hi naam, aur fresh browser profile.

Lesson 2.2: Sign up with a fresh email

Go to Etsy and click Register. Choose Continue with Google. Create a separate new Gmail for this account. Do not use a Gmail that already has an Etsy account. The email must not have any Etsy account on it. A reused email or reused details can cause trouble.

Nayi Gmail banayein jis par pehle se koi Etsy account na ho.

Lesson 2.3: Start the shop, then wait

Click Sell on Etsy, then Get started, then Start your shop. Etsy asks a general question about why you are here. Any answer is fine. After you register, leave the shop untouched for one day, ideally two days. Etsy needs time to check it. Do not rush to enter all details. Once the details are used, you cannot reuse them for another account if the first one is wasted.

Register karne ke baad shop ko ek ya do din haath na lagayein. Etsy ko check karne ka waqt dein.

Lesson 2.4: Country, language and currency

Set the language to English. Enter the shop country and currency correctly. Set Pakistan as the country. Do not choose the USA to look clever. Set Pakistan straightforwardly.

Country Pakistan likhein, USA nahi. Language English rakhein.

Lesson 2.5: Choose a shop name

Pick a brand-like name. It should fit your niche and be unique. You can ask ChatGPT for ideas. Tell it your niche and ask for 10 SEO-friendly shop name ideas. Etsy shows you when a name is already taken, so keep trying alternatives. You can also use your own name with your niche.

Shop ka naam brand jaisa ho, niche se match kare aur unique ho.

Lesson 2.6: Payoneer first

Payoneer must be created and fully verified before you make the shop. If you connect an unverified Payoneer account, Etsy can hold the shop and pause selling. Click Connect to Payoneer. If you already have one, choose I already have a Payoneer account and enter the details. Complete the authenticator step with an app like Google Authenticator. Payouts are first weekly, and after that daily withdrawal is possible. Payoneer account creation is a separate lesson in this module.

Payoneer pehle se bana aur verify hua ho. Bina verify kiye connect na karein.

Lesson 2.7: The fee and the card

Etsy charges a $19 shop setup fee. Use a card in your own name. If you do not have one, get one from any bank. If online use is not enabled, call the bank and ask them to turn on internet access. Tax also applies, so do not keep exactly $19 in the card. Keep a buffer above it. Repeated declined payments can risk suspension. The name on the card must match the name on Payoneer exactly, with the same spelling. If your CNIC is in Urdu, use the spelling shown on the bank account used for Payoneer. Fees can change, so check the current fees on Etsy before you publish.

Card apne naam ka ho, aur $19 se zyada balance rakhein, kyunki tax bhi lagta hai.

Lesson 2.8: First steps after the shop is created

When the shop is created, save the recovery codes shown on screen. They help if you have a problem with access later. When Etsy asks you to add a listing, you can choose Not now and add it later. Etsy Ads do not start at once. They become available about 15 days after the account is created. Then add a shop icon, banners, a shop title and a logo. Check shop violations and account settings in Shop Manager.

Shop banne ke baad recovery codes save karein, aur icon, banner aur logo add karein.

Lesson 2.9: Mistakes to avoid

  • Two accounts on one IP.
  • Reusing an email or details already used for Etsy.
  • Different name spellings on Payoneer, bank and card.
  • Choosing the USA instead of Pakistan.
  • Connecting unverified Payoneer.
  • Entering shop details at once, without the one to two day wait.
  • Keeping exactly $19 with no buffer for tax.
  • Starting without re-watching the steps.

Ye ghaltiyan na karein: do account ek IP par, purani email, alag alag spelling, aur bina tayyari ke shuru karna.

Lesson 2.10: Create a Payoneer account

Go to payoneer.com and choose Register. Enter your name, email address, phone number and country. In this lesson the country is Pakistan. Do not share your own details on screen.

Payoneer.com par jayein aur Register par click karein.

Lesson 2.11: Business details

For cross-border payment activity, choose that you are both sending and receiving payments overseas. For business type, choose sole proprietor, because you work alone. For employees, choose just yourself, or 1 to 2. For how you receive payments, choose online marketplace, because the payments are for Etsy. For which marketplace, type Etsy. You can add Fiverr too. For the expected value, choose an approximate figure. The example is $2,500. The exact choice does not matter much. Then continue.

Business type sole proprietor rakhein, aur marketplace mein Etsy likhein.

Lesson 2.12: Business registration and date of birth

Answer that the business is not registered, unless you have an LLC or another registered business. Then enter your date of birth and continue.

Agar LLC nahi hai to business not registered batayein, phir date of birth likhein.

Lesson 2.13: Address and phone verification

Enter the address exactly as it appears on your bank statement. Get the statement by email, or ask the bank to email it. Enter your phone number and request the code. The SMS code may arrive late. Do not worry. Use Resend code if needed.

Address bank statement jaisa hi likhein. SMS code late aaye to Resend karein.

Lesson 2.14: Password and security questions

Create a password of at least seven characters. It must have at least one letter and at least one number. Letters alone or numbers alone will not work. Choose and answer the security questions shown.

Password mein kam az kam ek letter aur ek number ho, aur saat characters se kam na ho.

Lesson 2.15: Identity document

Choose an identity document: CNIC, driving licence or passport. Enter your CNIC number. Enter your name in Urdu. If you cannot type Urdu, use Google Urdu Keyboard. Type the name there, then copy and paste it into Payoneer.

CNIC number aur naam Urdu mein likhein. Google Urdu Keyboard use kar sakte hain.

Lesson 2.16: Bank details

The CNIC details shown next must match the CNIC exactly. They cannot be changed. Choose a personal account, not a business account. Add a bank for receiving money. A regular bank works. Sadapay, Nayapay, JazzCash and Mobilink can also be used. For JazzCash, find the details in its app. Enter the IBAN, not the ordinary account number. A Pakistani IBAN starts with PK and has 24 characters. You can find it on a cheque book, or for Sadapay, under Load Money. Then submit the application.

IBAN likhein, account number nahi. Pakistani IBAN PK se shuru hota hai aur 24 characters ka hota hai.

Lesson 2.17: Verification and approval

After you submit, Payoneer shows review in progress and sends an email. Approval can take 24 to 48 hours. Payoneer may ask you to change a security question. Do that if asked. When approved, you get an email. If Payoneer asks for further verification, provide it. Once approved, the account is ready to use. This lesson covers creating and verifying Payoneer. The Etsy side is simple: connect it from the shop setup, as in Lesson 2.6.

Approval 24 se 48 ghante mein milti hai. Email ka wait karein.

Source: Free YouTube playlist (Account lesson and Payoneer lesson), Etsy Seller Handbook. Payment details must be checked on Etsy before this lesson is published.

Module 2 complete

Module 3: Product Idea, Keyword Research and Product Designing

Product idea, keyword research aur designing

Find a product idea. Check demand with keywords. Design the product.

  • How to find a digital product idea.
  • Keyword research: what buyers search for.
  • How to check demand and competition.
  • Designing in Canva: the basics.
  • File types buyers expect: PDF, PNG, Word and more.

Lesson 3.1: What is a keyword?

A keyword is the search phrase buyers actually type. Finding keywords means finding phrases that show real buyer demand. Before you choose any product, the first question is demand. Who wants it?

Keyword woh phrase hai jo buyer search mein likhta hai. Pehle demand check karein, phir product chunein.

Lesson 3.2: Demand first

People go to a market where a product has value. Sales are higher there. A product with no buyers in a place will not sell. The same applies to Etsy and every marketplace. Sales prove demand. One in-demand listing can matter more than many listings with no demand. Do not fixate on one product type, like T-shirts. Take any product, check whether it has sales and demand, and only then work on it.

Demand pehle, product baad mein. Jis product ki demand ho, usi par kaam karein.

Lesson 3.3: The A-B-C method

No tool is needed for this method. Use Etsy search itself. Type a base word, then a letter. For example, type table A. Etsy suggests phrases like table and chair. Those suggestions are keywords buyers are searching for. Repeat with B, C, D, E and so on. Table B suggests table behind couch. Do not copy only the example word table. Use any word for something you, or people around you, can make. It can be physical or digital. Repeat the same process for another base word. Design A gives design and crafted, design a mug, design bundles and creative company logo.

A-B-C method: base word ke baad A, B, C likhein. Etsy khud batata hai ke buyer kya search kar raha hai.

Lesson 3.4: Check demand for each suggestion

For each suggestion, open the results and check the sales, views and in baskets figures. These are demand signals. For example, a design bundles listing bought by two people, and a mug listing with 18 in baskets. These are real searches, not useless phrases. If people are searching for them, there is demand. Example from the lesson: a $2 digital T-shirt design listing with 51 sales, from a seller about two months old.

Har suggestion ke results khol kar sales aur baskets check karein. Wahan demand nazar aati hai.

Lesson 3.5: Quality over copying

Do not copy what others are doing. Taking an idea from one place and cutting and pasting it elsewhere creates problems. The product must be good quality and have value. If it is attractive and valuable, people will want to buy it.

Copy na karein. Product achha aur valuable ho to buyer khud aayega.

Lesson 3.6: Assignment: make a list of 10

After you choose a keyword or product, first ask whether you can make it. Write down 10 such keywords and products. Mark each one Yes if you can make it. Mark it No if you cannot. If a No item still has orders and demand, do not discard it. Find someone who can make that kind of work for you. Remember three things: the product must have value, it should not involve excessive work, and most importantly, it must have demand. Keep your keywords aside. The next lessons show how to use them.

10 keywords likhein. Har ek par Yes ya No likhein. Demand ho to kaam shuru karein.

Lesson 3.7: Why keyword research?

Demand alone is not enough. You also need to know how many sellers and buyers are in that market. Do not guess. That is what keyword research is for. The tool in this lesson is eRank. Before the tool, do a quick check on Etsy itself. Look at listings and how many people bought them. Even a small daily amount adds up. About $10 a day is about $300 a month. A product does not need huge daily sales to be worthwhile.

Demand ke saath ye bhi dekhein ke market mein kitne seller aur buyer hain. Is ke liye keyword research chahiye.

Lesson 3.8: How to use eRank

Start with a broad seed word. In the lesson the word is design. Set the market. The demo uses the USA. Other countries can be selected. Read the related keywords eRank returns. Note where the searches come from. In the example, about 12 percent were from the United States. US buyers can generally be charged more. Read two main columns: Search means average searches. Competition means how many sellers are already working on that keyword. Reject very high competition terms. Logo design is an example to ignore. A new seller cannot compete among so many sellers. Look for a low competition number instead. In the example it is around 20. Double click a keyword to open more detail. Check the colour signals. The competition indicator must be green. Other indicators may be orange. The ideal winning keyword has all four indicators green.

eRank mein seed word likhein, market chunein, aur low competition wala keyword dhoondhein. Competition green hona chahiye.

Lesson 3.9: What makes a winning keyword?

A winning keyword has real search demand and low competition. All four eRank indicators are green, and competition green is essential. It shows evidence of actual orders and buyers. It has a stable trend. Existing sellers earn reasonably from it. And it must fit what you can actually supply: physical, digital or print on demand. Repeat the process in your own field. Search the word that matches your skill: design, Excel, physical products, or anything else.

Winning keyword mein demand ho, competition low ho, aur chaaron indicators green hon.

Lesson 3.10: Worked example: custom logo stamp

The clearest example is custom logo stamp. It has low competition and green signals. It has a stable trend. Sellers get repeated orders, around 10 to 12 each in the examples shown. It is a good product to work on. But it is a physical product. It suits you only if you can handle physical fulfilment. Search by your own type. Physical sellers search physical products. Digital sellers search digital products. Print on demand sellers search that category.

Example: custom logo stamp. Low competition, green signals, aur repeated orders.

Lesson 3.11: Free eRank and auditing a competitor

eRank is a paid tool. Its free version gives five searches per day, with less detail than the paid version. Use each search carefully, one word at a time. Copy an exact phrase, like business stamp or business stamp custom, and search that exact phrase. eRank can also inspect a specific shop. Open a seller's listing and use the listing comparison and optimisation audit. The example listing earned well because its indicators were green and competition was low. Few people were working in that niche. Find that kind of low competition gap and use it.

Free eRank mein din mein paanch searches milti hain. Har search soch samajh kar karein.

Lesson 3.12: Start broad, expand, then validate

Start with a broad seed word. Ask what most buyers would actually type. For example, necklace. Most buyers search the simple word first. That is the starting point, not the final keyword. Expand it with ChatGPT. Ask for closely related terms, like choker style and pendant style necklaces. That list is only a guess. Check every term on eRank for real search data before you use it. Do the same with painting. Do not stop at the word painting. Buyers search specific phrases, like abstract painting or wall art for a living room. The specific phrase matches buyer intent better and faces less competition than the one word term.

Broad word se shuru karein, phir specific karein, aur har term eRank par check karein.

Lesson 3.13: How eRank is used

Use four parts of eRank. Keyword Explorer: enter a seed word and see the related keywords. Sort and filter them. Top Keywords: see what is being searched right now. Keyword Lists: save the keywords that pass the checks, so a product has a reusable list. Trend data and listing research: see how a keyword moved over time and which listings and shops rank for it. Compare the candidate keywords side by side. Do not choose by feel. Note: the video title mentions eHunt, but eHunt is not shown in this video. The tool taught here is eRank.

eRank mein Keyword Explorer, Top Keywords, Keyword Lists aur Trend data use karein.

Lesson 3.14: How to judge a good keyword

A good keyword is a balance, not just a big number. Enough search volume: people are actually searching for it. Manageable competition: a new shop should avoid terms full of established listings. A moderate volume, lower competition term is better than a huge, saturated one. Trend direction: rising or stable is good. A falling graph is a warning, even if past volume was high. Specificity and buyer intent: a longer, specific phrase that describes what the buyer wants beats a vague, high volume word. Relevance: it must describe the product you can actually deliver. Timing: seasonal terms only work if you list well before the peak. Legal risk: trademarked terms are not automatically safe. Check volume, competition and trend together, not one figure alone. Once chosen, the main keyword goes early in the title. Related keywords fill the 13 tags, attributes and description.

Achha keyword woh hai jismein volume ho, competition manageable ho, aur trend upar ya stable ho.

Lesson 3.15: Trending, seasonal and dead trends

Trending keywords show what is hot now, but check if the trend will last. Seasonal keywords spike at a fixed time. Christmas is the main example. Demand spikes late in the year, so prepare listings months ahead, not during the peak. Mother's Day gift keywords work the same way. A dead trend is a warning. Labubu was a craze with very high searches, but its trend graph collapsed. Entering a trend after it has peaked means competing for shrinking demand.

Trending keyword ki sustainability check karein. Seasonal listing peak se months pehle tayyar karein.

Lesson 3.16: Copyright and trademark keywords

Minecraft and Wicked are high demand but risky examples. Both are trademarked, brand owned terms. Putting such a term directly in a title or tags can lead to a listing being removed or a shop being suspended. Do not blindly copy a popular brand keyword. Work with generic or inspired designs and wording that does not use the protected brand name. Understand the risk before you use such a term at all.

Brand wale keywords se listing remove ya shop suspend ho sakti hai. Generic wording use karein.

Lesson 3.17: Reverse engineering: competitor is your friend

Do not guess. Study listings that are already selling. Open successful listings and check their titles, tags, photos and mockups, price, reviews, sales history and shop. Competitors have already done the research. Their titles and tags show which keywords are working. Their reviews show gaps and buyer complaints. Their pricing shows what buyers will pay. Learn from that and make a better, different listing on the same keyword. Better mockup, clearer title, better value. Do not copy the listing. Find current top sellers and top shops on eRank. Practice: pick a niche, run about 10 candidate keywords through eRank, keep only those with workable volume, competition and trend, save them in a Keyword List, and use them consistently in title, tags and description.

Competitor se seekhein, copy na karein. Behtar listing banayein.

Lesson 3.18: One design, four formats

The same design is sold in several formats: SVG, PNG, EPS and DXF. The design itself is the same. What changes is the file type. Digital files can be sold again and again, with no investment. SVG is the scalable vector format. It can be enlarged without pixelation. PNG is the high resolution raster image, with the background removed for transparency. DXF and EPS are additional vector formats buyers expect. DXF is for Cricut and laser cutting. EPS is the professional export format. DWG and PDF are optional extras.

Ek hi design chaar formats mein bikta hai: SVG, PNG, EPS aur DXF.

Lesson 3.19: Start with one clean AI image

AI images look fine at normal size. But they blur and break into pixels when you zoom in, because they are low resolution. Do not ask the AI tool to put two or four designs in a single image. Generate only one design in one AI image. Even a single image may still need its resolution improved.

AI se ek image mein ek hi design banwayein. Zoom karne par pixels toot jate hain.

Lesson 3.20: Make it high resolution in Photoshop

Open the low resolution image in Photoshop. Go to Edit, then Preferences, then Technology Previews, and turn on the two options shown there. Then click OK. Press Ctrl, Alt and I together to open Image Size. Choose Preserve Details and set the resolution to 300. Reduce noise only moderately. Too much noise reduction makes the image lose its detail. Click OK and let Photoshop upscale it. Zoom out and compare. The result is visibly clearer. Save the file with quality set to maximum.

Photoshop mein Image Size se resolution 300 karein, aur quality maximum par save karein.

Lesson 3.21: What is a vector, and the Pen Tool

Vectorising turns the raster image into a vector. A vector can be zoomed as much as you like without the pixels breaking. The first and most accurate method is the Pen Tool. It is in both Illustrator and CorelDRAW. Click to place points. Hold Alt to adjust a node. Drag to shape the outline until a shape is formed. Manual pen tracing is slow, but it is the most accurate method. For fine art, trace manually. For most Etsy work, auto trace is enough.

Vector ko jitna marzi zoom karein, pixels nahi tootte. Pen Tool sab se accurate hai.

Lesson 3.22: Auto-trace

Both CorelDRAW and Illustrator have automatic tracing. In CorelDRAW, select the image, click Trace Bitmap, then Outline Trace, then Detailed Logo. In Illustrator, import the file with Ctrl and O, or drag it onto the artboard while holding Shift. Click the image, then use Image Trace. For a black and white design, choose the Silhouette option and click OK. Auto trace saves time, but the shape comes out slightly distorted. Tracing quality depends on resolution. Always maximise the resolution in Photoshop first. Do not worry if the traced shapes are not exact. The buyer receives the design you made. An approximate but acceptable result is fine.

Auto trace waqt bachata hai, lekin shape thoda bigad sakta hai. Pehle resolution theek karein.

Lesson 3.23: PNG: remove the background

If you only need a PNG, you can simply remove the background in Photoshop. Use the Magic Wand tool. Press W. Click the black area, then choose Select Similar Color to select the same colour throughout. If colours differ, hold Shift and click them one by one. Do the same for a white background if white is dominant. Click the padlock on the layer to unlock it, then press Delete. The background becomes transparent. Save with File, then Save As.

PNG ke liye Photoshop mein Magic Wand se background delete karein.

Lesson 3.24: Remove white after tracing, then export

A plain Image Trace can leave a white background in the result. Use the Silhouette option, or use Expand, double click into the result, click each white background piece and delete it. If you cannot tell whether any white remains, select everything and change its colour. That reveals what is left. Finally set the design's colour to black. In CorelDRAW, right click and choose Ungroup Object, or press Ctrl and U, then delete the unwanted pieces and set the design to black. Then export. In Illustrator, go to File, then Export, then Export As. Make a folder for the files. Export DWG, then SVG, then DXF. EPS is not in Export As. For EPS, use File, then Save, then Save As, and choose EPS. You can also give a PDF and a PNG. In CorelDRAW, go to File, then Export, or press Ctrl and E. Choose SVG, tick Selected so only the selected design is exported, then repeat for DXF, DWG, EPS and PNG.

Trace ke baad white background delete karein, phir SVG, DXF, EPS aur PNG export karein.

Lesson 3.25: Gradient warning and copyright

Do not use gradients if you plan to auto trace. A gradient makes the tracer split the design into fragments of colour. Always ask the AI tool for a solid colour design if you want to auto trace it. And check copyright before making any design. That is the first thing to check.

Auto trace ke liye gradient use na karein. Solid colour design banwayein. Copyright pehle check karein.

Lesson 3.26: Prompt engineering first

A prompt is the instruction you give an AI tool. The tool generates an image from it. The wording controls the result. Good prompting is the core skill of this lesson, not manual drawing skill. You do not need to draw. You need to write a good prompt.

Prompt woh instruction hai jo aap AI ko dete hain. Achha prompt likhna hi asal skill hai.

Lesson 3.27: The AI tools

Three image tools are used, and no single one is compulsory. Ideogram is preferred in the demo. It is paid. ChatGPT generates images, and it also writes prompts from an existing image. Google Gemini is the free alternative for people who cannot pay for Ideogram. Gemini is also used for mockups. Experiment across tools rather than depend on one. Compare the outputs and pick the best. Complex mascot style designs cannot realistically be made in Canva alone.

Ideogram, ChatGPT ya Gemini, koi bhi use kar sakte hain. Gemini free hai.

Lesson 3.28: Download and convert the file

Download the generated image. Watch the file format. Images from ChatGPT may arrive as AVIF, which ChatGPT itself cannot read back. Convert AVIF to JPG or PNG with an online converter. Conversion takes a little time. If a tool gives JPG or PNG directly, no conversion is needed. You can also take a screenshot of the image. Making an SVG file is a separate lesson, covered in Lessons 3.22 and 3.24.

AVIF file ko JPG ya PNG mein convert karein, phir use karein.

Lesson 3.29: Reverse-engineer a prompt

Upload a reference image to ChatGPT. The free version allows uploading up to three images. Ask it to write a prompt for that image. Copy the prompt ChatGPT produces and paste it into Ideogram or another generator. ChatGPT will not always return exactly what you wanted. It may change things. The goal is a similar design, not an identical copy.

Kisi design ki image ChatGPT ko dein, us se prompt likhwayein, phir us prompt se naya design banayein.

Lesson 3.30: Similar, not identical

Do not copy a best-selling design exactly. Create something similar in style or theme, but different. Vary it further. Ask for a different theme, different wording, a different font, a white background, a different character or a different pose. Ask for changes in plain Urdu, or Punjabi, or by voice. Perfect English is not required. If the AI struggles, open a new chat, paste again, and let the generation finish before you interrupt it. You can also mix elements from more than one design for a blended result. Warning: if only small things are changed, like a cap and hands, copyright trouble can still arise. Keep asking the AI to make it different until you are happy with a clearly different version. Only then finalise it. Etsy allows AI made designs, but you must disclose AI use in the listing description.

Copy na karein. Similar banayein, lekin clearly different ho. AI use ki disclosure listing mein zaroor likhein.

Lesson 3.31: Listing mockups with Gemini

Once a design is downloaded and you like it, make mockups for the Etsy listing. Paste the chosen design into Gemini, use its image creation, and ask for a T-shirt mockup. If you cannot think of mockup wording, ask ChatGPT in Urdu to write four or five T-shirt mockup prompts, then use those. Try several: a girl wearing the T-shirt, a smiling girl, zooming on the design, a person holding the T-shirt, and a different angle. Check mockups carefully before you use them. A sad looking girl should not be uploaded. Check the focus on the design and realistic details, like wrinkles in the fabric. Practise, experiment, and go beyond the exact examples shown.

Mockup banane ke liye design Gemini mein dein. Mockup ko upload karne se pehle achhi tarah check karein.

Source: Free YouTube playlist (Module 3 lessons), Etsy Seller Handbook.

Module 3 complete

Module 4: Listing on Etsy

Listing karna

Your product is ready. Now list it the right way: title, description, tags, category, mockups and price.

  • Listing title: clear and simple, up to 140 characters.
  • Description: what to write first.
  • 13 tags: up to 20 characters each. Use all 13 slots.
  • Categories and attributes: fill every relevant field.
  • Mockups: how to show your product.
  • Pricing your digital product.
  • Etsy SEO: how search finds your listing.

Lesson 4.1: What is SEO?

SEO means search engine optimisation. Google and Yahoo are search engines. Etsy also has a search engine. Listings need to be optimised for it. A good product can still get no sales if its SEO is wrong.

SEO ka matlab hai search engine optimisation. Etsy ki bhi apni search hai.

Lesson 4.2: What Etsy SEO means

Etsy SEO means telling Etsy what the product is and which customer it should be shown to. The chosen keywords must appear in the title, description and tags. Then Etsy's algorithm can recognise the product and match it to a search. Keyword research only helps ranking when the researched words are actually placed where Etsy reads them. If you do not use the word for flowers in the title, a person searching for flowers will not see your listing.

Keywords title, description aur tags mein likhein, tabhi Etsy samjhega ke product kya hai.

Lesson 4.3: The title formula

The title is the most important element. Follow a three part structure. First, the main keyword. Second, the supporting keyword. Third, the use case and style. Example: Minimalist Abstract Wall Art is the main keyword. Modern Black White Poster is the supporting keyword. Living Room Home Decor is the use case and style. Etsy can combine parts of the title. Searches like minimalist wall art, abstract wall art and modern wall art can all match the same listing. Practise this structure. It gets easier over time.

Title teen hisso mein likhein: main keyword, supporting keyword, aur use case.

Lesson 4.4: Title rules

Put the main keyword at the start. Do not repeat keywords. Write a title that is readable and understandable for a human, not only for a robot. Example: Valentine Gift for Her. Valentine is the main keyword. Gift for her is the supporting phrase. It can match searches for Valentine, Valentine gift, gift for her, and the full phrase.

Main keyword shuru mein likhein, repeat na karein, aur title insaan ke liye readable ho.

Lesson 4.5: Tags strategy

Use all 13 tags. Split them like this. Five tags repeat the exact keywords used in the title. Five tags are related or similar keywords. Three tags are buyer intent keywords. Buyer intent means what the buyer wants. For example, gift for her or home decoration.

13 tags poori use karein: 5 title wale, 5 related, 3 buyer intent wale.

Lesson 4.6: Description SEO

Begin the description with the same title, with only a small change. Include the main keywords and the use case. A well written description helps Google as well as Etsy. Etsy listings can be indexed and appear in Google searches, because Google picks up the description data.

Description title se shuru karein, aur main keywords aur use case likhein.

Lesson 4.7: Images are silent SEO

Images are silent SEO. CTR means click through rate. Many products may be shown, but when a shopper clicks one, its CTR rises and Etsy pushes it more. So an image should be attractive enough to stop a scrolling shopper and make them click, even before sales arrive. Rules: clean background, lifestyle mockups, clear text, and a first image that acts as a scroll stopper.

Image achhi ho to buyer click karta hai, aur Etsy listing ko aur dikhata hai.

Lesson 4.8: Common SEO mistakes

Very short titles. Random or unrelated tags. Copy pasted descriptions. No clear niche. So many products in one listing that its niche is unclear. Not understanding trends, or chasing only one trend.

Ye ghaltiyan na karein: chhota title, random tags, copy paste description, aur unclear niche.

Lesson 4.9: Patience and testing

Etsy SEO is not magic. It is a game of data, patience and testing. It takes about one to two weeks for SEO to optimise. Sales do not normally arrive the day after a listing is made, except sometimes with low competition keywords. Collect data, be patient, keep testing, and sales will come.

SEO mein sabr chahiye. Ek do hafton mein result aata hai. Test karte rahein.

Lesson 4.10: Mockup videos with Comet AI

Sellers see T-shirt designs on models in polished mockup videos. They think they need many skills or expensive paid tools. The tool in this lesson is Comet AI from Perplexity. It is a browser like Chrome. Upload your own design into Comet and prompt it to make a T-shirt mockup of that design. Comet uses the same uploaded design, so the artwork stays recognisable. You can also ask it to place the design on the back of the shirt.

Comet AI se apne design ki T-shirt mockup banayein. Design wahi rehta hai.

Lesson 4.11: Model mockups and automatic prompts

Ask for a mockup in which a girl is wearing the T-shirt with your design. Comet does not just use the short instruction as written. It expands and polishes it into a fuller prompt by itself. That is a major advantage of the tool. One mistake to avoid: do not send the text prompt without re-attaching the design image. Send the image again together with the prompt. For example, ask for a mockup of a girl wearing a T-shirt with this design.

Prompt ke saath design ki image dobara attach karein, warna mockup nahi banega.

Lesson 4.12: From image to video

Download the mockup image. Open a new chat. Prompt Comet to make a video from this image. Comet writes its own detailed prompt. The resulting video looks realistic. The paid plan is $20 a month, as stated in the video, and it allows only five videos per month. So do not add a video to every Etsy listing. Use the generated images for most listings and reserve videos for selected listings. Generated images and videos can be cropped and reused. An unsatisfactory result can be regenerated.

Mahine mein sirf paanch videos milti hain. Video sirf selected listings ke liye use karein.

Lesson 4.13: Comet for titles and descriptions

Comet can also be used for listing SEO, like ChatGPT. Copy titles from other listings, paste them into Comet, and ask it to mix a new SEO-style title. Do the same separately for descriptions. Write your own final title and description in the end. Do not copy another seller's text word for word. The video says this will be explained in more detail in a later video.

Title aur description ke liye bhi Comet use kar sakte hain, lekin final text apna likhein.

Source: Free YouTube playlist (Module 4 lessons), Etsy Seller Handbook, How Etsy Search Works.

Module 4 complete

Module 5: Badges and Growth

Badges aur growth

How shops earn badges. How to fix common problems: views but no sales, reviews but no visits.

  • Bestseller badge: how a listing earns it.
  • Popular tag: what it means on a listing.
  • Star Seller badge: what it needs (check the current rules in the Seller Handbook).
  • Reviews are coming but visits are not.
  • Views and visits are coming but sales are not.
  • Shop age and the first sale: what to expect.

Lesson 5.1: The problem with Etsy Ads

A seller spends heavily on Etsy Ads and gets no orders. Many sellers have the same problem. Running ads without a strategy is giving Etsy money for nothing. Spending keeps rising while profit does not.

Bina strategy ke ads par paisa lagana Etsy ko paisa dena hai, sale nahi.

Lesson 5.2: Optimise the listing first

Do not start ads until the listing is optimised. Strong keyword research, an SEO optimised title, proper tags, high quality images, and a clear description. The keywords in the title and tags tell Etsy which searches to show the ad for. A weak image confuses a visitor. They leave after the click has already been paid for. A weak description fails to build trust, so the visitor goes back. Ask buyers for honest feedback. An early five-star review builds a new buyer's trust.

Ads se pehle listing optimise karein. Title, tags, images aur description theek hon.

Lesson 5.3: Small test budget

For beginners, use $1 to $3 per day and no more. Treat this as a test budget to learn from. Work out which listings get views, which get clicks, which get orders, and which are simply wasting budget. Do not set an ad running and leave it. Analyse the funnel from views to clicks to orders.

Shuru mein $1 se $3 roz ka budget rakhein. Test karein aur seekhein.

Lesson 5.4: Test several listings for 7 days, then scale

Run ads on 5 to 10 listings for at least 7 days. Ads need time to collect data. At first they are shown broadly. Then the platform gradually learns exactly who to show them to. Then identify the best listings and scale them up by increasing their budget. Switch off ads on listings that only take clicks and waste money. Scale only a listing that gets both clicks and orders.

5 se 10 listings par 7 din ads chalyein, phir winner ka budget barhayein.

Lesson 5.5: The biggest mistake: stopping after 2 days

The biggest mistake is turning ads off after one or two days out of fear. The first five to seven days are needed to collect data. Stopping early means learning nothing and repeating the waste. If an ad is not performing, switch it off and restart it after a week, then run it for seven days. But if it is giving sales, leave it alone.

Do din baad ads band na karein. Pehle saat din data collect karne ke liye chahiye.

Lesson 5.6: Pro tips and the formula

Use high demand keywords with many searches. Make attractive images. Test multiple listings rather than putting ads on only one. A different listing may be the one that performs. Before increasing spending, change the main images. Keep pricing in line with a similar top listing. Do not undercut drastically. Selling for $1 what competitors sell for $10 spoils the market. Selling for $9 is a modest reduction. Spend more on ads for listings that are already selling organically. Etsy has already tested those listings and buyers' trust in them is building. Only what buyers want sells. The formula is: SEO plus strategy plus ads equals sales.

Formula yaad rakhein: SEO plus strategy plus ads barabar sales.

Lesson 5.7: Earnings are not the point, the roadmap is

The lesson opens with a big day: $800 in one day. The question people ask most is how much the teacher earns. The answer in the lesson is simple. How much he earns should not matter to you. What matters is whether he gives you a usable roadmap. That roadmap is what the free course gives. You can learn for free, because everything is available on YouTube. Mentorship is only for learners who get stuck in many places and cannot understand from YouTube alone. In that case, a mentor answers questions and guides you step by step.

Kamai nahi, roadmap zaroori hai. Free course se seekhein, mentorship sirf tab jab atak jayein.

Lesson 5.8: The example shown

The lesson shows the teacher's own Etsy stats for 17 November to 5 December 2025. In that period: 8,083 visits, 1,292 orders, a 16 percent conversion rate, and revenue of $2,534.53. Daily orders grew from 3 to 416 across the days shown. Daily revenue grew from $6 to $800 a day. This is from digital products. The lesson also shows students reporting sales, including one who got a first sale three days after starting with only six products. This is an example shown in the lesson, not a promise. Your results depend on your product, your effort and the market.

Ye example hai, waada nahi. Aapka result aapke product aur mehnat par depend karta hai.

Lesson 5.9: Community and mentor

Fix your community first. At the start, always put your community right. The better your community, the better your outcome. If you stay among negative people, you will only get negativity. Thumb rule for choosing a mentor: earning a lot of money does not mean someone is a good teacher. A good mentor comes down to the learners' level and explains things in a way they can understand. A teacher is someone who can make students understand. It is about mindset, not money.

Community pehle theek karein. Achha mentor woh hai jo aapki level par aa kar samjhaye.

Lesson 5.10: Diagnose why there are no sales

Many beginners complain about zero sales. First ask whether the shop is getting views and visits. If traffic is coming in, the problem is probably not SEO. It is inside the listing itself. Most likely the pricing or the description is not right.

Sale nahi aa rahi to pehle dekhein ke views aa rahe hain ya nahi. Views hain to masla listing ke andar hai.

Lesson 5.11: Three kinds of demand

Learn three kinds of demand. Evergreen products get searches every month and stay fairly stable. Example: bookmark SVG. Seasonal products return every year. Example: Christmas. Searches were lower in September, then rose, then fell again. Sellers who prepared in September were ready for the October and November sales period. Searches were already lower in December and almost absent in the middle of the year. The past trend predicts when demand will rise and fall. Trending products appear for a short time and then disappear. Example: Labubu. Even correctly made listings can fail if trends are ignored. That is the biggest overlooked reason for no sales.

Demand teen tarah ki hoti hai: evergreen, seasonal aur trending. Trend check kiye bina listing fail ho sakti hai.

Lesson 5.12: Timing: start 2 to 3 months early

Buyers search and buy in advance. Just as a sacrificial animal is bought before Eid, not after it, and Eid or Christmas preparations happen beforehand, Etsy buyers also search and buy in advance. Beginners may work on trends, but should mainly build on evergreen products and at least on seasonal ones. Start seasonal work two to three months before the event. Halloween is on 31 October, but searches mainly came in September, with little after October. So stop working on Halloween after it passes. The same applies to Eid shopping. Buyers try to order a week, a fortnight or a month early in case of holidays or delivery delays.

Seasonal kaam event se 2 se 3 mahine pehle shuru karein. Buyer pehle se khareedta hai.

Lesson 5.13: List every day

Many people create a single listing and then wait passively. That will not work. The habit is one new listing daily. After that, orders should follow. Use the community for motivation and answers. When people post daily about getting sales, it motivates others. Many questions can be answered there too.

Roz ek nayi listing lagayein. Ek listing bana kar intezar karna kaam nahi karta.

Source: Free YouTube playlist (Module 5 lessons), Etsy Seller Handbook. Badge rules change, so they must be checked in the Seller Handbook before this lesson is published.

My Journey

Mera safar

I share what I learn, one post at a time. Follow the journey from zero.

My Etsy Journey — From Zero to 40 Sales

40 sales completed — 19 November 2026

My Etsy journey started with a simple idea, back in March, at a small learning session in Mailsi, Punjab, Pakistan.

I had already been providing services to local clients for more than three and a half years. That session inspired me to take my work to the international marketplace.

Within just one month, I received my first sale. It was an unforgettable moment. I felt that I was finally moving in the right direction.

But things didn't go as I expected. Sales were inconsistent, and I started questioning my decisions. I thought perhaps Etsy wasn't working for me.

I started experimenting in different directions. I thought attractive designs alone would bring sales, but I was missing something very important. Proper research, branding, and a clear direction.

Then I made an important decision. I joined a course, and for the first time, I started understanding what I had been doing wrong. Two major problems became clear. I didn't know how to research products properly, and I didn't know how to identify the right competitors.

I realized that my original niche was the right direction. Mixing different categories had been a mistake. So I started cleaning up my shop, removing unrelated listings, and focusing again.

During my third phase, I started using AI more intelligently. I learned that AI can become a powerful research assistant when we give it clear instructions and the right prompts. I used AI to discover keywords and improve my research process, and this time, I started seeing better results.

With better research, a clear direction, and consistent effort, my shop started moving forward. And today, Alhamdulillah, I have reached 40 sales.

Forty sales may be a small number for some people, but for me, it represents learning, mistakes, patience, consistency, and the courage to start again.

If you're struggling with your Etsy journey, don't give up. Learn from your mistakes, improve your research, and keep moving forward. Because success is not just about making sales. It's about becoming better with every step.

LEARN. RESEARCH. IMPROVE. NEVER GIVE UP.

میری ایٹسی کی کہانی — صفر سے 40 سیلز تک

40 سیلز مکمل — 19 نومبر 2026

میری ایٹسی کی کہانی ایک سادہ سے خیال سے شروع ہوئی تھی، مارچ میں، پنجاب کے چھوٹے سے شہر میلسی میں ایک چھوٹی سی سیکھنے کی نشست میں۔

میں ساڑھے تین سال سے زیادہ عرصے سے مقامی کلائنٹس کو اپنی خدمات دے رہا تھا۔ اسی نشست نے مجھے متاثر کیا کہ میں اپنے کام کو عالمی مارکیٹ تک لے جاؤں۔

صرف ایک مہینے کے اندر مجھے میری پہلی سیل ملی۔ یہ ایک ناقابلِ فراموش لمحہ تھا۔ مجھے لگا کہ آخرکار میں صحیح سمت میں آگے بڑھ رہا ہوں۔

لیکن چیزیں ویسے نہیں ہوئیں جیسی میں نے سوچی تھیں۔ سیل کبھی آتی، کبھی نہیں، اور میں اپنے فیصلوں پر شک کرنے لگا۔ مجھے لگا شاید ایٹسی میرے لیے نہیں ہے۔

میں نے مختلف سمتوں میں تجربے شروع کر دیے۔ مجھے لگتا تھا کہ خوبصورت ڈیزائن ہی سیل لے آئیں گے، لیکن میں ایک بہت اہم چیز بھول رہا تھا — صحیح تحقیق، برانڈنگ، اور ایک واضح سمت۔

پھر میں نے ایک اہم فیصلہ کیا۔ میں نے ایک کورس جوائن کیا، اور پہلی بار مجھے سمجھ آنے لگا کہ میں کیا غلط کر رہا تھا۔ دو بڑے مسائل سامنے آئے — مجھے نہیں آتا تھا کہ پراڈکٹس کی صحیح تحقیق کیسے کی جائے، اور نہ ہی یہ کہ صحیح حریفوں کو کیسے پہچانا جائے۔

مجھے احساس ہوا کہ میری اصل نِش ہی صحیح سمت تھی۔ مختلف کیٹیگریز کو ملانا ایک غلطی تھی۔ تو میں نے اپنی شاپ کی صفائی شروع کی، غیر متعلقہ لسٹنگز ہٹائیں، اور دوبارہ فوکس کیا۔

اپنے تیسرے مرحلے میں میں نے مصنوعی ذہانت کو زیادہ سمجھداری سے استعمال کرنا شروع کیا۔ میں نے سیکھا کہ جب ہم اسے واضح ہدایات اور صحیح پرامپٹس دیں، تو یہ ایک طاقتور تحقیقی معاون بن سکتی ہے۔ میں نے اسے کی ورڈز دریافت کرنے اور اپنی تحقیق بہتر بنانے کے لیے استعمال کیا، اور اس بار مجھے بہتر نتائج نظر آنے لگے۔

بہتر تحقیق، واضح سمت، اور مسلسل محنت کے ساتھ میری شاپ آگے بڑھنے لگی۔ اور آج، الحمدللہ، میں 40 سیلز تک پہنچ چکا ہوں۔

چالیس سیلز کچھ لوگوں کے لیے ایک چھوٹی سی تعداد ہو سکتی ہے، لیکن میرے لیے یہ سیکھنے، غلطیوں، صبر، مستقل مزاجی، اور دوبارہ شروع کرنے کی ہمت کی علامت ہے۔

اگر آپ اپنی ایٹسی کی کہانی میں مشکل کا سامنا کر رہے ہیں، تو ہار نہ مانیں۔ اپنی غلطیوں سے سیکھیں، اپنی تحقیق بہتر بنائیں، اور آگے بڑھتے رہیں۔ کیونکہ کامیابی صرف سیلز بنانے کا نام نہیں — یہ ہر قدم کے ساتھ بہتر بننے کا نام ہے۔

سیکھو۔ تحقیق کرو۔ بہتر بنو۔ کبھی ہار نہ مانو۔
